entry.figure_title: Anterolateral ligament injury and adjacent meniscotibial attachment
entry.alt: Original Figure 4 separates ultrasound A/C on the left from coronal MRI B on the right; solid arrowheads mark the abnormal anterolateral ligament, an outlined arrowhead marks the nearby lateral meniscotibial ligament insertion, and an asterisk identifies meniscal body.
entry.caption: Source injury example in a 31-year-old man with recent knee sprain and full-thickness ACL tear. MRI B is a coronal fat-saturated T2-weighted turbo-spin-echo 3 T image: solid arrowheads mark thickening and waviness of the anterolateral ligament; an outlined arrowhead marks the lateral meniscotibial ligament beside its tibial plateau insertion. A is ultrasound from the injured knee; C is contralateral ultrasound with normal ALL appearance. The contralateral normality claim does not apply to MRI B or the whole injured knee.
entry.source_caption_full: Fig. 4 ALL tear in a 31-year-old male patient with a recent knee sprain and full-thickness ACL tear. A Longitudinal 22-8 MHz US image and ( B) coronal fat-saturated tSE T2-weighted 3 T scan show thickening and wavy appearance of ALL (arrowheads). Note the lateral meniscotibial ligament (outlined arrowhead) inserting into the tibial plateau in close proximity to ALL. C Longitudinal 22-8 MHz US from the contralateral knee of the same patient demonstrates the normal appearance of ALL (arrowheads). Outlined arrowhead, meniscotibial ligament; asterisk, meniscal body. The inserts illust rate the respective probe position
entry.image_state: ALL injury example with adjacent meniscotibial attachment; target-specific meniscotibial integrity is not reported
structures_visible: Anterolateral ligament (locally thickened and wavy, solid arrowheads)
Lateral meniscotibial ligament (outlined arrowhead at tibial plateau attachment)
entry.limits: Only MRI B is selected for clinical-image scope. The author labels local ALL thickening/waviness and the nearby lateral meniscotibial insertion; one slice does not establish either complete course, attachment footprint, physical tissue dimensions or independently verified integrity. No statement in the source establishes the meniscotibial ligament as normal or injured. ACL rupture belongs to the patient context and is not directly illustrated or credited by this selected MRI slice. Ultrasound A/C, including contralateral normal appearance in C, cannot satisfy MRI requirements or transfer normality to B. Side, MRI slice thickness, voxel spacing, TR/TE and complete examination findings are unreported.
